key_insight: To understand why language-model data attribution fails, evaluations need to separate the effects of different dataset properties. This paper introduces the Controlled Attribution Benchmark (CATT) to support that diagnosis through fact tracing.
problem_solved: Existing evaluations change multiple dataset properties at once, making it difficult to identify why methods succeed or fail at linking a model’s factual outputs to its training data.
method: Explore the design space of language-model data attribution, focusing on evaluation.
Introduce CATT, a controlled benchmark for tracing facts to training data.
Use controlled evaluation to disentangle potential causes of attribution failure; the provided abstract is truncated before the experimental details.
impact: More diagnostic evaluations could help practitioners choose and improve attribution methods rather than rely on aggregate task scores. The provided excerpt does not include results establishing particular methods’ strengths or weaknesses.
visual_elements: Flow diagram: training data → language model → factual output → attributed source.
Side-by-side comparison: multiple dataset properties changing together versus controlled changes.
Conceptual benchmark dashboard showing dataset-property controls and attribution performance, without invented results.
Magnifying-glass icon highlighting the goal of diagnosing attribution failures.
paper_title: Elucidating the Design Space of LM Data Attribution
paper_authors: Steven Yu, Sheng-Yu Wang, Kimia Hamidieh, Antonio Torralba, David Bau
